title: Amritsar Man Shot Dead Outside Home After Argument Over Parked Scooter
excerpt: Police name three brothers from the same neighbourhood after Amit Sabharwal was shot five to six times in Anand Avenue; no arrests yet.
body:
• Amit Sabharwal, 27, was shot dead outside his home in Amritsar's Anand Avenue on Friday night after an argument over moving a parked Activa scooter, police said.
  • Gate Hakima SHO Baljinder Singh said Abhi Shah fired five to six pistol rounds; police have named three brothers — Abhi, Sunny and Hritik Shah, neighbours of the victim — in the case.
  • No arrests had been made as of Saturday; police are examining CCTV footage and conducting raids.
  • The killing drew a political attack from BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu, who said law and order had completely collapsed in Punjab.

A young man was shot dead outside his home in Amritsar's Anand Avenue after an argument over a parked scooter, police said on Saturday. The victim was identified as Amit Sabharwal.

Gate Hakima Police Station SHO Baljinder Singh said police were informed on Friday night by the victim's father, Sunil Sabharwal. According to the SHO's account carried by ANI via LatestLY, Amit arrived outside his home with a friend, where their Activa scooter was parked. Three brothers from the same neighbourhood — Abhi Shah, Sunny Shah and Hritik Shah — arrived and asked for the Activa to be moved to the side. An argument followed, after which Abhi Shah allegedly fired about five to six rounds from a pistol at Amit, killing him.

"No arrests have been made yet. Raids are being conducted, and the perpetrators will soon be apprehended and put behind bars."

— Baljinder Singh, SHO, Gate Hakima Police Station

Investigation under way

Police said they are examining footage of the incident and conducting raids to arrest the accused. No arrests had been made as of Saturday afternoon. The three named accused are residents of the same neighbourhood as the victim, according to police.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2113969513037447453

Separate coverage of the case notes that Amit, 27, worked in marketing at a private firm, and that his father said he had no known enemies. Those details, and the family's account that he was shot by people known to him, are now part of the police investigation; the motive beyond the parking dispute has not been established by police.

Political reaction

The killing triggered a political row over law and order in Punjab. BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu, in a post on X, called the shooting spine-chilling and said law and order had "completely collapsed" in the state. He asked when Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, who also holds the home portfolio, would take responsibility.

The state government had not issued a response in the reports available on Saturday. The case adds to a series of violent incidents reported across Punjab in October that have kept policing and public safety at the centre of the state's political argument ahead of next year's elections.

What happens next

Police say arrests are the immediate focus, along with recovery of the weapon and verification of the CCTV record. Until the accused are in custody and a chargesheet is filed, the sequence of events rests on the police account given by the SHO and the family's statement. Further updates are expected once raids conclude.
